target: Mae ganddo fo gi du.
english: He has a black dog.
tip: After the 'have' word ganddo, the owned thing soft-mutates: ci (dog) becomes gi in Mae ganddo fo gi du.

target: Addawodd hi na fyddai'n hwyr.
english: She promised she wouldn't be late.
tip: Reported 'that... not' uses na plus mutation: byddai turns into na fyddai (that she wouldn't) after Addawodd hi.

target: Paid â phoeni am wneud camgymeriadau.
english: Don't worry about making mistakes.
tip: After â in a command, p becomes ph: poeni turns into Paid â phoeni (don't worry).

target: Paid â brysio, cymer dy amser.
english: Don't rush, take your time.
tip: cymer is the informal singular command 'take', from cymryd: cymer dy amser (take your time).

target: Mae'r ffilm hon cystal â'r llyfr.
english: This film is as good as the book.
tip: cystal is the special 'as good as' form of da, used with â: cystal â'r llyfr (as good as the book).

target: Mae'r parc yn agos at y llyfrgell.
english: The park is near the library.
tip: 'Near' pairs with at, not i: yn agos at y llyfrgell (near the library).

target: Bydd hi'n bwrw glaw yn hwyrach heno.
english: It will rain later this evening.
tip: Welsh 'to rain' is bwrw glaw, literally 'to strike rain': Bydd hi'n bwrw glaw (it will rain).

target: Mae'r ardd mor brydferth â llun.
english: The garden is as beautiful as a painting.
tip: mor (as/so) soft-mutates the next word: prydferth becomes brydferth in mor brydferth â llun (as beautiful as a painting).

target: Mae'r bwyd cartref yn flasusach na bwyd y caffi.
english: Home food is tastier than café food.
tip: Add -ach for 'more' and follow with na for 'than': yn flasusach na bwyd y caffi (tastier than the café food).

target: Peidiwch â bwydo'r merlod gwyllt!
english: Don't feed the wild ponies!
tip: Peidiwch â is the plural or polite 'don't'; Paid â is for one person: Peidiwch â bwydo (don't feed).

target: Mae angen moddion arna i.
english: I need medicine.
tip: Welsh puts the need on you. Mae angen moddion arna i is literally medicine is a need on me, meaning I need medicine.

target: Mae'r dyddiau'n mynd yn hirach.
english: The days are getting longer.
tip: mynd yn plus an adjective means becoming. Here mynd yn hirach means getting longer, not simply going somewhere.

target: Mae'n well gen i gerdded na gyrru.
english: I prefer walking to driving.
tip: Mae'n well gen i means I prefer, literally it is better with me, so mae'n well gen i gerdded is I prefer walking.

target: Pa lwybr sy'n mynd i ben yr Wyddfa?
english: Which path goes to the top of Snowdon?
tip: Pa, meaning which, softens the next consonant, so llwybr becomes lwybr in Pa lwybr, which path.

target: Os gorffenna i'r llyfr, bydda i'n ei fenthyg i ti.
english: If I finish the book, I'll lend it to you.
tip: For a real if, Welsh uses Os with a future verb. Os gorffenna i means if I finish, then bydda i, I will.

target: Byddwn i wedi galw pe bawn i'n gwybod dy fod di adref.
english: I would have called if I'd known you were home.
tip: Byddwn i wedi galw means I would have called. Pair it with pe bawn i, if I were, for the unreal past condition.

target: Mae'n gas gen i smocio.
english: I hate smoking.
tip: Mae'n gas gen i means I hate, literally it is hateful with me, so mae'n gas gen i smocio is I hate smoking.

target: Mae Cymraeg yn anoddach na Ffrangeg.
english: Welsh is harder than French.
tip: The ending ach makes comparatives, so anodd, hard, becomes anoddach, harder, in Mae Cymraeg yn anoddach.

target: Y fferm sy ger y llyn.
english: It is the farm that is near the lake.
tip: Fronting a subject adds emphasis. Y fferm sy ger y llyn means it is the farm that is near the lake.

target: Mae llawer o bethau i'w gwneud yma.
english: There are lots of things to do here.
tip: After llawer o, lots of, the next word softens, so pethau becomes bethau in llawer o bethau.

target: Byddai'n well gen i gerdded yn hytrach na gyrru.
english: I'd prefer to walk rather than drive.
tip: yn hytrach na means rather than. Byddai'n well gen i gerdded yn hytrach na gyrru is I'd rather walk than drive.

target: Mae'r gwanwyn yn dod â'r ŵyn bach i'r caeau.
english: Spring brings the little lambs to the fields.
tip: To bring is dod â, literally come with. Mae'r gwanwyn yn dod â'r ŵyn means spring brings the lambs.

target: Pe baen nhw wedi gwybod, bydden nhw wedi helpu.
english: If they had known, they would have helped.
tip: Pe baen nhw means if they had, and bydden nhw wedi helpu means they would have helped, the unreal past pattern.

target: Os bydd hi'n bwrw eira heno, bydd y ffyrdd yn beryglus.
english: If it snows tonight, the roads will be dangerous.
tip: Welsh weather uses bwrw, to cast. Bwrw eira literally casts snow and means to snow, as in Os bydd hi'n bwrw eira.

target: Bwyton ni bysgod a sglodion wrth yr harbwr.
english: We ate fish and chips by the harbour.
tip: The object of a short-form verb softens, so pysgod, fish, becomes bysgod in Bwyton ni bysgod.

target: Mae Osian yn smwddio'i grys ar gyfer y cyfweliad.
english: Osian is ironing his shirt for the interview.
tip: His here is 'i, tucked after the verb, and it softens crys to grys in smwddio'i grys, ironing his shirt.

target: Drwy ddarllen, dysgais i.
english: Through reading, I learned.
tip: Drwy (through, by) softens the next word, so darllen becomes ddarllen in Drwy ddarllen.

target: Addysg sy'n agor drysau.
english: It's education that opens doors.
tip: To stress the doer, put the noun first and add sy'n: Addysg sy'n agor drysau (education is what opens doors).

target: Mae angen i fi gynilo.
english: I need to save.
tip: Mae angen i fi plus a verb means 'I need to' do it: Mae angen i fi gynilo (I need to save).

target: Mae'r ffordd osgoi ar gau.
english: The bypass road is closed.
tip: ar gau is the fixed phrase for 'closed' (roads, shops): Mae'r ffordd osgoi ar gau.
